author: KChito_Review
quote:
Plenty of graphical muscle, but little of the GTA soul

After more than a decade of waiting and an astronomical budget, we are left with an experience that beneath its spectacular visual polish is weighed down by baffling design choices and a sleep-inducing pace. Rockstar seems to have forgotten what made its games fun, opting instead for a heavy-handed realism that slows down every action.

The biggest drawbacks lie in the gameplay and the pacing. The opening in Leonida Keys feels endless, and the story takes far too long to truly get going once you finally reach Vice City. Midway through the campaign, the narrative stalls, bogged down by repetitive tasks aimed at accumulating money and reputation, while the conclusion feels rushed. Furthermore, the simulation-heavy approach inherited from *Red Dead Redemption 2* is a poor fit for this formula: the controls are clunky, melee combat remains awkward, and managing minor interactions such as opening a car trunk or picking up items is unnecessarily slow.

Compounding this are several cutbacks that are hard to justify after so many years of development. The inability to freely purchase businesses, the absence of classic activities, and most notably the inability to replay missions directly from the pause menu are clear steps backward compared to previous entries.

Technically, the visual leap is undeniable, but the price is high: being locked to 30 FPS with noticeable drops during intense action sequences completely **** the fluidity, which is unacceptable in 2026. When you add in questionable business practices such as selling a "physical edition" that contains only a download code, or locking side activities behind special editions the final impression is bittersweet. A technical marvel, certainly, but a step backward as a video game.

author: KChito_Review
quote:
Marvel’s Wolverine tenía todos los ingredientes para convertirse en uno de los grandes juegos de acción de PS5: un personaje tremendamente carismático, un estudio como Insomniac Games detrás y la posibilidad de explorar un lado mucho más oscuro y violento del universo Marvel. Sin embargo, el resultado deja una sensación bastante decepcionante.
El principal problema es que el juego parece tener dificultades para encontrar su propia identidad. Wolverine es un personaje que debería transmitir brutalidad, fuerza y peligro, pero buena parte de la experiencia termina sintiéndose demasiado previsible y convencional. Golpear enemigos puede resultar espectacular durante los primeros compases, pero la fórmula acaba haciéndose repetitiva.
El sistema de combate es probablemente uno de los aspectos que más podrían entusiasmar al principio. Las garras, las ejecuciones y las habilidades de Logan permiten crear momentos bastante espectaculares. El problema aparece cuando llevas varias horas jugando y empiezas a darte cuenta de que muchas situaciones se resuelven de una manera muy similar.
Falta una sensación de verdadera evolución. Wolverine debería sentirse cada vez más poderoso y peligroso, pero el progreso no siempre consigue transmitirlo. En lugar de convertir el combate en una experiencia cada vez más profunda, el juego parece confiar demasiado en el espectáculo visual.
Además, el diseño de algunos enfrentamientos resulta poco inspirado. Hay momentos en los que parece que el juego está obligando a Wolverine a enfrentarse a grupos de enemigos simplemente para alargar la duración.
La historia intenta presentar una versión más adulta y oscura del personaje, algo que sobre el papel resulta muy atractivo. Sin embargo, el tono serio no siempre viene acompañado de una narrativa igual de sólida.
El problema no es que la historia sea mala en sí misma, sino que en determinados momentos resulta excesivamente previsible. Algunos personajes parecen estar ahí principalmente para hacer avanzar la trama y no porque tengan realmente algo interesante que aportar.
También se echa en falta una mayor sensación de riesgo. Wolverine es un personaje perfecto para una historia violenta y emocional, pero el juego no siempre consigue aprovechar todo su potencial.
Otro de los puntos que menos convencen es la exploración. El escenario puede parecer impresionante visualmente, pero tener un mundo atractivo no significa necesariamente que sea interesante recorrerlo.
Hay zonas que dan la impresión de existir simplemente para colocar combates, objetos coleccionables o pequeñas actividades secundarias. Después de jugar durante un tiempo, explorar deja de sentirse como una parte importante de la aventura y empieza a parecer una forma de rellenar el mapa.
Visualmente, Marvel’s Wolverine demuestra el potencial de PS5. Los modelos de personajes, las animaciones y los efectos durante los combates pueden ser impresionantes.
Pero los gráficos no pueden solucionar los problemas de diseño. Un juego puede verse espectacular y, al mismo tiempo, tener una estructura repetitiva.
Y precisamente esa es una de las sensaciones que deja esta aventura: que en determinados momentos estamos viendo una demostración técnica de lo que puede hacer una PS5, más que jugando a una experiencia realmente memorable.
Quizá el mayor inconveniente sea precisamente que el protagonista es Wolverine.
Con un personaje así, las expectativas son enormes. No basta con ponerle garras, hacerlo sangrar y permitirle regenerarse. El jugador debería sentir constantemente que está controlando a uno de los personajes más salvajes y carismáticos de Marvel.
En algunos momentos esa sensación está ahí. En otros, sin embargo, Logan parece simplemente otro protagonista de un juego de acción en tercera persona.
Y cuando un juego protagonizado por Wolverine consigue hacerte olvidar durante un rato que estás jugando como Wolverine, algo no termina de funcionar.

Conclusión

Marvel’s Wolverine no parece un mal juego, pero sí una oportunidad desaprovechada.
Tiene un protagonista extraordinario, un apartado técnico potente y momentos de acción capaces de ofrecer auténticos espectáculos. Sin embargo, el combate puede hacerse repetitivo, la exploración no siempre aporta demasiado y la historia no consigue mantener de principio a fin el nivel de intensidad que debería tener una aventura protagonizada por Wolverine.
Es un juego que puede entretener, pero que debería haber aspirado a mucho más.

author: KChito_Review
quote: The "open world" is empty, boring, and unrewarding to explore. Furthermore, the new mechanics feel like filler and add nothing. The level design is awful and offers no incentive to explore. To top it all off, the constant presence of secondary characters telling you what to do completely undermines the solitary and mysterious exploration typical of the series.

author: KChito_Review

It doesn't innovate much in terms of open-world design: it feels very familiar and, in some ways, conservative. Furthermore, the game's pacing slows down in certain sections, especially toward the end. There are times when the story feels predictable or less **** the other hand, the AI ​​is quite poor.

author: KChito_Review
quote: Honestly, Silent Hill f on PC left me with mixed feelings. On the one hand, it's visually very powerful and the setting is engaging, but there are several technical details that mar the experience. What bothered me most were the cinematics locked at 30 fps, which are very noticeable when you're coming from a smooth game. I also experienced the occasional crash, and it seems the game requires a lot of VRAM; if your graphics card is limited, you'll notice **** interesting detail: disabling motion blur breaks the image, so you're basically forced to play with it enabled even if you don't like it. What's more, it only officially works on Windows 11, which excludes those still using Windows **** for the design, towards the end it overuses the action and the boss fights feel repetitive, which somewhat undermines the essence of Silent **** short: it's enjoyable, but on PC it suffers from technical limitations and some annoying bugs that make it feel less than polished.

author: KChito_Review
quote: When I started playing the game I already knew that it wasn't going to be spectacular, but what I didn't know was that it was going to be worse than I expected. Technology is supposed to advance and offer us more and more spectacular things, but that's not the case. It's a regression in all aspects, gameplay, visuals and sound. Games from past generations far surpass this game, and everything you can see in the game is pure theater, every element is nailed to the ground with the idea that it's a flower vase, objects, NPCs that don't react to anything... etc. I don't know if the combat was intended to be an RPG or a Tekken combat due to the load of effects and colors. It's slow, it feels rough like games from several decades ago, Risen or Gothic, in short, a disaster in all aspects. If we add to all this that it's completely broken and full of bugs, then it ends up burying this game. It's impossible for me to recommend such a disastrous game.

author: KChito_Review
quote: It's been a while since I played such a perfect platform game. The artistic design, levels and overall technical aspects are quite good for a minor game. Very replayable and with many extras, you can't ask for more.

author: KChito_Review
quote: This game is supposed to be better than the previous one, but nothing could be further from the truth. Textures take a long time to load or objects appear very abruptly on the ground, on the other hand we have game freezes for several seconds, things that didn't happen in the previous game.

author: KChito_Review
quote: It feels rough, it seems like a game that hasn't evolved at all. The artificial intelligence could be greatly improved and let's not even talk about the story, which is simple and boring. On top of all this, there are all the bugs that still need to be fixed.

author: KChito_Review
quote: I had a lot of doubts about this remake, and I was very wrong. The game not only respects the original 1:1, but it expands on it and goes beyond. The entire original game has been enhanced, graphics, music and gameplay. To say something negative, the performance leaves a lot to be desired, I hope they fix it as soon as possible.

author: KChito_Review
quote: A 10/10 game, devilish gameplay, amazing graphics that immerse you in Chinese mythology, the sound section is not far behind, the music of the time makes you teleport to that place.

author: KChito_Review
quote: Seriously? How long of a wait for this? Saying it's more of the same would be very generous. Already in the first installment the story was very slow and boring, with an absurd combat system, unfortunately this game not only repeats its same mistakes but if you didn't play the first installment you won't learn anything.Again, a story that tells nothing, what good are those open scenes if you then move through them in a straight line like a hallway? 6 hours of hallways and screams, it could pass for a horror game instead of an adventure.This is the first game with a 4k texture mod and little else, yes, the water effect is very spectacular, little more. But if even the character of Senua seems to have the same number of polygons, so much so that they sold us that he was the most beast on a technical level, what a time wasted.
